title: FancyZones crashes when using Shift key to activate zones

fix_assessment.rationale: The original report includes a video and a diagnostic archive, and a second user now reproduces a similar regression on two PCs with PowerToys 0.97.0 and 0.102.3001 after 0.91.1 worked. This establishes a reproducible regression, but the available evidence does not identify whether the disappearing overlay is a stale Shift state or a broader FancyZones hang.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore reliable Shift-drag activation after the 0.91.1 regression
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A regression in the Shift-drag activation path or its interaction with FancyZones state is plausible. Current code tracks Shift through both low-level keyboard-hook handling and Raw Input, but the issue evidence does not prove which transition or component causes the overlay and editor to stop responding.
plan: Reproduce on PowerToys 0.102.3001 with Shift-drag enabled and compare the same setup with 0.91.1, recording whether the overlay disappears and whether the layout editor remains responsive.

Trace the Shift transitions through FancyZones::OnKeyDown/OnKeyUp, FancyZones::OnKeyboardInput, DraggingState::SetShiftState, and WindowMouseSnap::MoveSizeUpdate in the failing and last-working builds.
Fix only the confirmed stale-state or stalled-component transition and add a regression test that verifies both zone activation and subsequent layout-editor responsiveness.
verification: Run the reproducer on a built-in FancyZones layout with Shift-drag enabled on a current stable build and on 0.91.1 for comparison.
Verify that the zone overlay remains available while Shift is held, snapping completes, and the layout editor continues to open after repeated drags.
Run the focused FancyZones Shift-drag UI tests, including the existing Shift-drag activation and drag-toggle cases.

confidence.rationale: Two users report the same post-0.91.1 failure and the current source has a multi-input Shift-state path, but no current trace or source-level failing transition ties that path to the observed hang.

issue_context.summary: Holding Shift while dragging briefly shows FancyZones zones, then the overlay disappears and FancyZones stops responding until toggled or restarted.
known_information: The original reporter identifies PowerToys 0.92.0 on Windows 10 build 19045, reports 0.88.0 through 0.91.1 working and later versions failing, and supplied a bug-report ZIP and video.
The original report says disabling Windows Snap does not change the failure and the layout editor works before the failure.
A second user reports the same Shift-drag failure on two HP all-in-one PCs with 0.97.0 and 0.102.3001, while 0.91.1 works; that user's layout editor also stops working after the failure.
The second user's report says the issue occurs with the built-in Columns layout and that toggling or restarting FancyZones restores it temporarily.
inferences: The version comparison from both users supports a regression introduced after 0.91.1, but does not locate the introducing change.
Because the second user's layout editor also becomes unresponsive, the failure may extend beyond the zone overlay or Shift-state calculation.
issue_context.analysis: The repro is now independently confirmed across two users and multiple versions, so another generic reporter-log request would not add much. Current FancyZones code sets Shift through low-level hook handling and Raw Input, while DraggingState::Enable reseeds the state from GetAsyncKeyState; WindowMouseSnap updates highlights when snapping mode changes. These are investigation points, not proof of the fault. Reproduce the reported version transition and inspect state/event flow before choosing a code change.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue report, original video and bug-report reference, plus the November 5 confirmation with version comparison and additional editor failure.
Inspected FancyZonesLib/DraggingState.cpp, FancyZonesLib/FancyZones.cpp, and FancyZonesLib/WindowMouseSnap.cpp for Shift-state activation and overlay updates.
Inspected existing FancyZones UI tests for Shift-drag activation and drag-toggle behavior; they do not establish the reported hang.

judgment.rationale: The original report and a second user's cross-version reproduction establish a repeatable Shift-drag failure; the specific defect mechanism remains unconfirmed and should be investigated by maintainers.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the same Shift-drag sequence on 0.91.1 and current stable, then trace the Shift-state and overlay path before implementing a fix.
evidence: The original report supplies a video, a bug-report reference, and a 0.91.1-versus-later version comparison.
A second user independently confirms the failure on two devices with 0.97.0 and 0.102.3001, and reports the layout editor becomes unresponsive.
Current source has distinct low-level hook and Raw Input paths that update the Shift state, but no failing transition has been confirmed.

actions.label: Compare Shift-drag on 0.91.1 and current stable

reproduce.title: Reproduce FancyZones Shift-drag regression
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare PowerToys 0.91.1 with current stable 0.102.3001 or newer on Windows 10 and Windows 11 where available.
prerequisites: Enable FancyZones and the setting to hold Shift to activate zones while dragging.
Use the built-in Columns layout and a normal, non-elevated Explorer window.
steps: Start with PowerToys 0.91.1 and hold Shift while dragging the window across a zone; record whether the overlay remains visible and the window snaps.
Repeat the same steps on current stable without changing the layout or display setup.
After the overlay disappears, try opening the FancyZones layout editor and record whether it still responds.
Repeat several drags to determine whether toggling FancyZones only restores one attempt or restores sustained operation.
reproduce.expected_result: The overlay stays available while Shift is held, the dragged window can be snapped, and FancyZones settings and the layout editor remain responsive after repeated attempts.
